result.rationale: The server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema in addGuests.schema.ts is `z.object({bookingId: z.number(), guests: z.array(z.string().email())})` with no uniqueness refine, unlike the client's ZAddGuestsInputSchema in AddGuestsDialog.tsx which refines for uniqueness. The handler's uniqueGuests filter only checks `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` — it does not deduplicate within the guests input itself — so duplicate emails in one request would be inserted twice. The described mechanism is verifiable from the diff.

judged_text: ZAddGuestsInputSchema validates email format but drops the uniqueness requirement that the client-side refine in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29 enforces, leaving the directly callable tRPC mutation without it. An authenticated caller posting guests: ["a@x.com","a@x.com"] passes the server schema, and the handler filter (which only compares against existing attendees) inserts two identical BookingAttendee rows and sends the same guest two AttendeeScheduledEmail invitations.

adjudication.rationale: The server-side input schema in `addGuests.schema.ts` only enforces `z.array(z.string().email())` and does not include the client’s uniqueness `refine` from `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters only against existing attendees / blacklist, not duplicates within the incoming `guests` array, so `guests: ["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` can result in `createMany` being called with duplicate entries. If the DB allows it, this would create duplicate attendee rows; additionally `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` uses the original (non-deduped) list and will email per attendee entry in `calendarEvent.attendees`, so duplicated attendees can lead to duplicate invite emails.
